purpose: Screen published AI-image detector candidates before downloading large weights or changing product decisions.

environment_constraints.operational_requirement: A candidate must support a bounded, short-lived CPU inference process and independently auditable assets before it can enter an offline evaluation.
environment_constraints.safety_context: Previous concurrent Python model work caused a high-memory application failure, so unbounded large-model loading is excluded.

candidates.name: AIDE
observations: The upstream README specifies CUDA 11.8 and distributes checkpoints only through a Google Drive folder.
No publisher checksum was supplied for the checkpoint link.
The model builds ConvNeXt-XXLarge and the official evaluation path calls model.cuda() and torch.cuda.synchronize().
candidates.reason: No hash-verifiable weight chain and no safe CPU evaluation path in the published implementation.

candidates.name: LASTED
observations: The published dependency list targets torch 1.9.0 and clip 1.0.
Pretrained weights and datasets are served via Google Drive; the README requests a license form for the associated test data.
No publisher checksum is listed for the pretrained detector weights.
candidates.reason: The pretrained asset cannot be independently verified and the published environment is materially older than the local runtime.

candidates.name: UniversalFakeDetect / UnivFD
observations: The local OpenAI CLIP ViT-L/14 file is SHA-256 b8cca3fd41ae0c99ba7e8951adf17d267cdb84cd88be6f7c2e0eca1737a03836 and its bundled downloader verifies the publisher hash.
The upstream validation script forces CUDA, but the backbone itself can load on CPU.
Existing local controls report original AUC 0.28 and JPEG-75 AUC 0.12666666666666665; mean AI scores are lower than real scores.
candidates.reason: It fails the local control screen and is not a useful complementary signal.

candidates.name: AntiFakePrompt
observations: Official inference requires frozen Vicuna 7B weights in addition to the prompt-tuned checkpoint.
Published checkpoints are Google Drive downloads with no listed cryptographic checksum.
The dependency size exceeds the bounded CPU worker budget.
candidates.reason: The full VLM stack is not safe or practical for this CPU-only desktop inference path.

candidates.name: C2P-CLIP
candidates.source_license: not stated in the upstream repository root
observations: The official README distributes pretrained models via Google Drive and lists no checkpoint checksum.
The stated inference checkpoint is trained on GenImage and has no local transformed-real calibration result.
candidates.reason: No explicit reusable license or hash-verifiable detector checkpoint, so it cannot enter an auditable product evaluation.

candidates.name: GAPL
candidates.source_license: not stated in the source repository root
observations: The public checkpoint is 1.22 GB and uses PyTorch pickle serialization; the model also requires a separate CLIP ViT-L/14 backbone.
models.py hard-codes an author-local Linux Hugging Face cache path and uses local_files_only=True.

inference_image.py selects a CPU device when CUDA is unavailable, but instantiates GAPLModel without passing that device; the model constructor defaults to cuda and moves the backbone before inference can proceed.
candidates.reason: The published single-image path is not CPU-reproducible and would require multi-gigabyte unbounded memory before a first score.

candidates.name: FusionDetect / AIGI-Holmes / RIGID / WaRPAD / SSAFE
observations: FusionDetect's official repository currently says Coming Soon and has no implementation or weights.
AIGI-Holmes publishes a 15.1 GB model and documents multi-GPU vLLM inference.
For RIGID, WaRPAD, and SSAFE this audit found papers but no official runnable pretrained implementation and checksum-verifiable model release.
candidates.reason: No bounded, reproducible CPU inference asset is currently published.

conclusion: No screened candidate is eligible to change Demirror's AI conclusion. This is a negative research result, not evidence that the remaining detectors are sufficient.
